jobs.description:
The Meta Infra Technical Program Management (TPM) community is pioneering technologies to bring people and businesses closer together at a global scale. Infra TPMs are the enablers for our toughest business strategies to become technical realities, requiring direct and close partnership with both Engineering and Product teams to make products come to life with incredible scale, reliability, and efficiency.Meta's infrastructure software stack is being upgraded for a world where the primary consumer of our platforms is an agent, not a human at a terminal, and our core infrastructure stack is being upgraded for the rigor, speed, and scale required of modern training, inferencing, and app development. These shifts change how we design APIs and interfaces, how we onboard and support internal and external partners, how we plan features, and how we measure adoption and success. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own that transformation for a major surface of Meta's Infra software stack.In this role, you will partner with Engineering and Product leadership to shape the technical roadmap for the platforms you own, drive the design and rollout of the interfaces those platforms expose, and own end-to-end delivery and adoption with the partner teams who build on top of them. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy on ambiguous, cross-organizational problems turning open-ended strategic questions into concrete programs with a credible path to success and you will set the technical program management standard for the teams around you.

Technical Program Manager, Infrastructure Software Systems Responsibilities:

Own technical program management for a core area of Meta's infrastructure software stack, spanning platform strategy, technical design, delivery, and partner adoption
Partner with Engineering and Product to define the multi-quarter roadmap: shaping feature plans, participating substantively in technical design and API/interface design reviews, and making tradeoff recommendations that leadership acts on
Drive platform adoption end to end — defining the onboarding path for partner teams, removing friction in integration, and holding the bar on the partner experience from first evaluation through steady-state production use
Translate the needs of demanding internal customer organizations into platform requirements, and broker the prioritization conversations required to land them
Define and instrument the metrics that determine whether the platform is succeeding — adoption, reliability, efficiency, and developer/agent effectiveness — and use them to drive decisions rather than to report status
Lead technical discussions and act as a thought leader in program and design reviews
be the cross-functional partner engineering leaders pull into their hardest problems
Identify and solve systemic problems that span organizational boundaries, and build the lightweight operational constructs that accelerate team momentum without adding overhead
Perform risk assessment, risk mitigation, and change management across a portfolio of concurrent technical programs
Articulate technical vision, requirements, goals, and milestones to stakeholders up to and including VP-level leadership
Provide hands-on program management through design, development, testing, rollout, and post-launch phases
Mentor and raise the bar for other technical program managers, and influence how TPM is practiced across the broader organization

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience
10+ years of experience in software, systems, or hardware engineering, or technical product/program management
Experience delivering technical programs or products from inception through to delivery
Knowledge of user needs assessment, requirements gathering, and scope definition
Experience working autonomously across multiple teams, demonstrating critical thinking and thought leadership
Experience communicating and collaborating with technical management teams to develop systems, solutions, and products
Experience in organization, coordination, and prioritization of competing workstreams
Experience in analytical thinking and problem-solving applied to large-scale systems
Experience establishing and maintaining working relationships across multidisciplinary teams and with partners in multiple time zones

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience partnering with large internal customer organizations to migrate them onto a shared platform
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Experience supporting AI/ML infrastructure — training, inference serving, or the software layers that sit on top of them
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
Experience building or operating agent-facing platforms, tooling, or APIs, including agent orchestration and evaluation
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Model Delivery
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own model delivery.

Every model we ship, whether we trained it or brought it in from a partner, has to be selected on evaluation criteria, integrated and routed across the product stack, and adhere to regulatory requirements; released to customer environments ready for general availability. That now happens on a monthly cadence, with several model evaluations a week, and each release goes out to our platform partners.

This is a standing program, with one owner from model candidate to GA. You will join Product Engineering Program Management and work across modeling, evaluation, inference serving, engineering, customer delivery.

At Cohere, Technical Program Managers are the operational owners of cross-functional work. The best of them are precise at the tactical level and useful at the strategic one: organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic, and able to change pace when the program does.

As a Technical Program Manager, You Will

Own the path from model candidate to general availability for first-party and third-party models, on a monthly cadence.
Build one release process across modeling, evaluation, product integration, and customer delivery, with an owner, exit criteria, and lead time for each stage.
Run a delivery-readiness gate that has to pass before general availability: packaging, signed images and digests, documentation, serving configuration, test coverage, and parity across Platform, Model Vault, and private deployments.
Work with Safety and Legal to build regulatory checkpoints into the model release pipeline, including EU AI Act systemic-risk obligations. Program manage the recurring compliance calendar post launch: the yearly review of our frontier framework, serious-incident reporting deadlines, and access for external evaluators.
Stand up a model registry the field, partner teams and regulators can answer from, covering name, route, alias, checkpoint, sizing, serving configuration, and where each model is available.
Run intake for new models, keep the pipeline visible, and drive the selection decision to the right owner by a date, with a decision log of which models enter the lineup.
Sequence deprecation and partner notices on a calendar agreed with customer and partner teams.
Make the monthly model lineup change a routine step in North, including routing and availability, and feed model readiness into the product release train.
Build the mechanisms that make the cadence repeatable: templates, the registry, automation, and retros that change the system.
Write the status, the decision, and the external notice so executives, engineers, and partners are working from the same answer.

You May Be a Good Fit If You

Have at least 8 years as an Engineering or Technical Program Manager, including ownership of repeatable launches with readiness checklists, go/no-go gates, and rollback criteria that teams actually used.
Can discuss model serving and deployment at a working level: GPU sizing, tensor parallelism, quantization, speculative decoding, containers, Kubernetes and Helm, image signing, and air-gapped or private deployment. Enough to spot conflicting answers and know who decides.
Drive open questions (name, alias, default, sizing) to the owner who should decide them, by a date, and then publish the answer.
Influence without authority across research, engineering, product, and the field.
Write clearly for executives, engineers, and external partners, including customer and partner notices.
Are comfortable at a high cadence, with shifting priorities and overlapping launches.
Can read evaluation results and a cost-versus-performance tradeoff, and can tell when a benchmark does not answer the product question.

Helpful, And Not Required

Launch experience at a model provider or an AI platform.
Familiarity with the ML lifecycle: evaluations, checkpoints, provenance, and serving stacks such as vLLM.
Experience running launches under regulation or an AI management standard, such as the EU AI Act or ISO 42001.
Experience with model routing, AI gateways, or agent platforms.
Enterprise software delivery to regulated customers.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

An established organization seeks a technically grounded cybersecurity professional to assess proposed technologies, enterprise applications, artificial intelligence solutions, cloud platforms, and third-party vendors prior to production use. This position serves in a technical advisory and assessment capacity, focusing on security reviews rather than hands-on engineering, security operations center operations, audit, or traditional governance, risk, and compliance. Define review scope, identify security requirements, and ensure necessary validation activities are completed.
Evaluate architecture artifacts, including network diagrams, data flow diagrams, integration patterns, API designs, vulnerability assessments, and assessment documentation.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience:
Approximately 5 to 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology, software engineering, solution architecture, risk assessment, or a related discipline, with at least 5 years assessing or delivering applications, cloud services, integrations, APIs, or enterprise technology solutions.

Strong understanding of modern application security, cloud security practices, and secure software development lifecycles. Role Overview

As Technical Project Manager
, you will plan and drive complex, cross-team delivery across the engineering organization. You will help shape scope, timing, and phasing with Customer Success, Product, and Engineering, then own the path from plan to successful release: translating goals into actionable plans, surfacing dependencies and risks early, and maintaining forward momentum across teams. This technical role requires sufficient understanding of architecture, integrations, and environments to ask critical questions, challenge estimates, and help engineers resolve blockers.

Key Responsibilities

Lead planning for cross-team initiatives and releases, converting scope and goals into milestones, sequencing, and clear ownership while partnering with engineering leads to break down work, validate estimates, and reflect real capacity.
Run engineering ceremonies and delivery cadences, including sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, retrospectives, dependency reviews, and release readiness reviews; establish and enforce clear definitions of ready and done.
Track progress and maintain roadmaps, epics, and boards in Jira and related tools; identify and resolve blockers early, escalating through established paths when necessary.
Understand system architecture, data flows, integrations, and environments to map cross-team and third-party dependencies with designated owners and dates; maintain a living risk log covering likelihood, impact, mitigation, and ownership.
Coordinate release, cutover, rollback, and deployment plans with Engineering and DevOps, and partner with Quality Engineering to align validation plans and exit criteria prior to committing deadlines.
Provide clear status and tradeoff visibility regarding scope, timing, and quality to leadership, Product, and Customer Experience teams, translating technical details for non-technical stakeholders and supporting customer implementation commitments.
Partner with engineering leadership to refine planning, estimation, capacity management, and delivery practices across product lines; define metrics such as predictability, cycle time, and dependency lead times, and conduct retrospectives to mitigate recurring delays.
Utilize AI-assisted tools where they enhance planning, reporting, or coordination, applying appropriate review to verify outputs.

Required Qualifications

6+ years of experience in technical project management, program management, software engineering, or a related technical delivery role, including 3+ years managing cross-team software initiatives.
A track record of delivering complex SaaS releases on time by building realistic plans, managing dependencies, and adapting as conditions change.
Enough technical depth to understand system architecture, APIs, integrations, environments, and CI/CD workflows, and to engage credibly with engineers on design and estimation.
Experience running Agile delivery (Scrum, Kanban, or a hybrid) and adapting processes to fit the team rather than the other way around.
Proficiency with Jira or comparable tools for planning, tracking, and reporting on work across multiple teams.
Ability to identify, quantify, and communicate risk, and to drive decisions on scope, timing, and quality tradeoffs.
Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to give concise status to executives and detailed direction to engineering teams.
Comfort leading through influence: aligning people who do not report to you around shared plans and priorities.
Strong organizational skills and follow-through, with a habit of making ownership and next steps explicit.

Preferred Qualifications

Domain Expertise: Background in energy, utilities, grid management, or regulated sectors with extended customer sign-off cycles.
Enterprise Implementation: Proven success deploying enterprise software or complex integrations for large clients alongside continuous core product releases.
Scale & Governance: Track record of maturing delivery processes or establishing project management frameworks within expanding SaaS organizations.
Technical Tooling: Working knowledge of modern tech stacks such as TypeScript, Node.js, React, PostgreSQL, and AWS.
Roadmapping & Collaboration Tools: Proficiency with Confluence, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, or equivalent platforms for documentation and cross-functional alignment.
AI Integration: Experience leveraging AI-driven tools to enhance planning, status reporting, and cross-team coordination.
Professional Certifications: PMP, PgMP, CSM, SAFe, or equivalent credentials.

Accordingly, this role is restricted to individuals who qualify as “U.S. persons,” defined by federal law as U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), asylees, or refugees.

Professional development opportunities

What you will do How do we manage 15x more buildings with just 2-3x more people?
That's the challenge our Operational Excellence team is here to solve.
Our ambition is simple: make every team at Thermosphr dramatically more productive, by combining the smartest people, processes, and technologies. We believe talented people should spend their time solving interesting problems, not drowning in repetitive, low-value tasks.
Your mission?
Get your hands dirty, challenge how things work, and build better ways of doing things across the company.
Make our operations scalable.
Rethink how we deploy buildings, manage information, coordinate teams, and deliver our services, so that growing 10x doesn't mean working 10x harder.
Eliminate low-value work.
Simplify workflows, cut unnecessary steps, and automate repetitive tasks. Make sure our people spend their talent where it really counts.
Turn ideas into results.
Take ownership of your initiatives, bring people on board with Operations, Product, Sales and other teams, and drive implementation until you get real results.
Build, test, iterate.
Experiment with AI, automation, no-code tools, and software integrations. Prototype solutions, put them into people's hands, learn what works, and keep improving.
Win people over.
Bring teams along from day one, support them through the change, and keep going until adoption is real and the gains are measurable.
Think cutting weeks off building deployments, building an AI-powered assistant for internal teams, or automating a workflow that currently eats up hours of someone's week.
No endless recommendations or PowerPoint strategies. We want people who make things happen.

Strong analytical skills and confidence working with data and digital tools.

new_jobs.description:
About the Role

AppGate Professional Services is looking for a customer-focused Customer Delivery Project Manager to lead the implementation of our Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform for US commercial customers. As the primary customer-facing lead for medium to large engagements, typically two to six months long, you will own delivery from project handover through production go-live and transition to Support and Customer Success.
This is a delivery leadership role, not a sales or account management position. You will manage scope, schedule, budget, deliverables, and expectations across structured, milestone-driven projects, working alongside AppGate engineers so they can stay focused on architecture, configuration, and customer enablement. Professional Services operates as a P&L, so this role directly influences project profitability, revenue realization, and services margin. Success is measured by on-time milestone delivery, customer satisfaction at go-live and close-out, project financial performance, and clean handover to Support with complete close-out documentation.

Key Responsibilities

Customer and Stakeholder Management

•Serve as the primary AppGate point of contact for US commercial customers throughout service delivery, managing day-to-day requests and communication.
•Build strong working relationships with customer IT and security teams, project sponsors, and executive stakeholders.
•Lead status calls, milestone reviews, and stakeholder briefings so all parties have a clear, accurate view of progress, risks, and decisions required.
•Manage expectations proactively, addressing scope, timeline, and deliverable questions before they become escalations.
•Translate customer requests into actionable delivery tasks, assess feasibility, flag out-of-scope requests, and route them to the right internal resource.
•Escalate risks and customer concerns early, with a clear recommendation.

Delivery Execution

•Manage multiple concurrent ZTNA implementations across US commercial customers.
•Own service delivery end to end: scope, schedule, budget, milestones, deliverables, and resource coordination.
•Maintain delivery documentation throughout each engagement, including project plans, status reports, risk logs, and go-live and close-out records.
•Coordinate AppGate delivery engineers on each project, ensuring clear task ownership and removing blockers.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Software Quality Operations (SWQOps) team is at the heart of ensuring the safety, reliability, and quality of the Waymo Driver. Our mission is to build an adaptable and scalable operation, increasingly powered by AI, to deliver the crucial insights necessary to confidently deploy and grow Waymo's autonomous vehicle service.

Why This Team Is Essential To Waymo's Success

Waymo is undergoing unprecedented growth, rapidly expanding into new cities (targeting ~20 new cities by EOY 2026) and launching new vehicle platforms. SWQ Ops plays a critical role in this expansion, making it possible to scale safely and efficiently. The Regulatory Reporting Operations team within SWQ Ops owns the scaled delivery of datasets and methodologies used to evaluate events of regulatory interest and ensure reporting accuracy as Waymo continues to scale. We are on the front lines of:

De-risking New Deployments: Through meticulous triage of driving and simulated events, issue discovery, and continuous field monitoring, SWQ Ops provides early warnings and critical insights. This "early intervention in RO issue detection" ensures operational resilience and safety, particularly in new and complex environments, which is critical as Waymo enters multiple new cities and ramps up platforms like Ojai.

Driving Engineering Velocity: By handling the vital work of performance evaluation, issue deep-dives, and data set curation, SWQOps collaborates heavily and allows Waymo's Engineering, SysEng, Simulation, and Data Science teams to focus on their core tasks of developing and improving the Waymo Driver.

new_jobs.description:
At Amentum
, we're not just solving problems; we're engineering the future. Our team is driven by an unyielding commitment to innovation, integrity, and collaboration, tackling some of the most significant challenges in science, security, and sustainability. If you're passionate about making a real impact and want to be part of a community that values ethical excellence, this is the place where your ambition can thrive.

Here, we believe that success comes from continuously pushing boundaries and working together to deliver on our promises. We embrace challenges with confidence and are dedicated to creating a secure and vibrant future for all.

We’ll inspire and empower you to deliver your best work so you can evolve, grow and succeed – today and into tomorrow. We offer an exciting range of opportunities to develop your career within a supportive team who always strive to do the right thing for our people, clients and communities.

People are our greatest asset, and we offer a competitive package to retain and attract the best talent.

In addition to the benefits you’d expect, UK employees also receive free single medical cover and digital GP service, family-friendly benefits such as enhanced parental leave pay and free membership of employee assistance and parental programmes, plus reimbursement towards relevant professional development and memberships.

Work-life balance and flexibility is a key focus area for us. We’re happy to discuss hybrid, part-time and flexible working hours, patterns and locations to suit you and our business.

About The Opportunity

The announcement of a planned 20-year lifetime extension for Sizewell B is much more than an energy story. It is a significant investment in people, skills, local communities and the UK's long-term energy resilience. Sizewell B will continue generating electricity until 2055, extending its original operating life by two decades. For Suffolk and the wider East of England, this represents a major opportunity to build on an already strong nuclear legacy while creating lasting economic and social value for generations to come.

Since entering service in 1995, Sizewell B has been one of the UK's most reliable sources of low carbon electricity. Today, the station generates enough power for around 2.5 million homes.

At a time when energy security remains a national priority, extending the life of an existing nuclear plant makes strategic sense. Nuclear generation provides stable, around-the-clock electricity regardless of weather conditions, complementing the growing contribution from renewable energy sources.

To support this significant project Amentum are recruiting for a number of experienced Project Manager's to join our Nuclear Power Engineering and Technical Services team supporting our key client EDF Energy Nuclear Generation with their nuclear fleet in the UK.

These are key role's within our project and engineering portfolio which is spread across our UK network at all UK sites and stations. You will be supported and mentored by experienced project engineering management professionals within the business and given the training and opportunities you need to develop and expand your project engineering management and leadership skills with larger and more complex projects.

You will be part of a large client-led team at Sizewell B Power Station and will be accountable to the client Project Manager, Programme Manager and/or Construction Manager. Flexible working arrangements between office and home may be possible, however the role will predominantly be based at the Power Station.

Key responsibilities will be:

Project Managers are accountable to the client PPM for successful delivery of all aspects of their assigned projects. The Project Manager sets the project execution strategy in agreement with the client PPM and uses a cross-functional project team to deliver the project safely in line with company policies and procedures, achieving established goals and objectives within the agreed baseline. This role has no direct reports
The role will be based at the EDF Sizewell B Power Station and will require occasional business travel to other UK sites/stations. In this role you will report to the business Operations Manager but be accountable for project delivery directly to the client
Everyone working in our team will have a proven track record of working within highly regulated environments with high safety standards and culture
Strong communication and organisational skills are a must with the ability to develop relationships and maintain effective networks and be results-focused tempered with a team-centred approach.

Qualification, Skills & Experience

Degree educated, ideally in engineering or a related subject, with preferred Chartership
APMP formal project management qualification or equivalent and versed in modern project management techniques within complex, multi-functional organisations; have a thorough understanding and knowledge of engineering, design, procurement, safety case, construction and iinstallation / commissioning management and commercial contracting
Able to demonstrate an understanding of Safety Cases including how they are developed and implemented, relevant Health and Safety and Environment legislation including CDM and the actions required to achieve compliance
Good understanding of the needs of quality and how quality is assured and controlled along with relevant experience of commercial, contractual, and financial project drivers
Demonstrable experience of managing projects throughout the full project lifecycle, ideally across a range of complex multi-discipline projects and environments, and management of an integrated project team including staff, agency and assigned functional support
Experience of estimating, cost control, planning and commercial awareness including the preparation of business cases and sanction/ funding papers
Experienced in the preparation of reports and information using packages such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint, be proficient in the use of estimating, scheduling, programming and risk tools and in the use of Earned Value tools. Analytical approach with high-level problem-solving ability
Experience of working at Power Stations and Nuclear Licensed Sites is preferred but not essential

Our Culture

Our values are built on a strong foundation of safety, integrity, and respect for every individual. People are at the heart of our mission, and we believe in supporting one another through a culture of care and collaboration.

We strive to create a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. Supporting mental wellbeing and fostering a sense of connection are essential to how we work.

When we embrace different perspectives and work together, we become more innovative, more agile, and more successful.

We partner with VERCIDA, for greater online accessibility please visit www.vercida.com to view and access our roles. Regular travel is essential to build stakeholder relationships, assess readiness, support implementation planning, and help organisations manage risks and dependencies as they prepare for PeoplePortal adoption.

As rollout activity increases between 2028 and 2030, you'll play a key role in delivering consistent support throughout the readiness and implementation journey. Experience of ESR and workforce systems would be beneficial.

27 days leave (increasing with length of service) plus 8 bank holidays

Hybrid working model
Career development
Active wellbeing and inclusion networks
Excellent pension
NHS Car lease scheme

Support delivery of regional readiness and implementation activities, contributing to programme objectives and operational planning.

new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

Come be a part of a fast-paced, fulfilling and fun team in beautiful Colorado Springs, CO! Odyssey is looking for high-performing, passionate people ready to make a difference by joining our existing team of dedicated professionals supporting Space Domain Awareness.

We have an exciting new opportunity providing Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS) supporting the US Space Force mission to defend National Security Interests in Space as a Space Surveillance Telescope (SST) Sustainment Program Manager
providing Program Support as a member of the SST System Program Office (SPO) in Combat Forces Command (CFC), Mission Delta 2 (MD2), Second Sustainment Squadron (2STS).

The SST is a 3.5m aperture wide field of view telescope located near Howard E. Holt Naval Station in Australia. Its mission is to synoptically search the area of regard over the telescope and discover objects in orbits ranging from low-Earth (LEO) to cis-lunar. Discoveries are correlated against known satellite catalogs (also known as the tactical order of battle), with this tracking data then shared with Command and Control (C2) centers in Australia and the US. The SST is remotely operated out of a combined sensor operations center near Perth, Australia.

2STS is the U.S. Space Force organization responsible for sustaining and modernizing resilient space capabilities supporting Battle Management, Command, Control, Communication, and Space Intelligence (BMC3I). 2STS synchronizes sustainment efforts with Mission Deltas to improve mission readiness and works together with Space Systems Command (SSC) on acquisition efforts for critical space system capabilities for CFC.

Odyssey provides support to the Government in five areas: Product Support, Sustainment Engineering & Sustainment Management, Technical Order Management, Technical User Interface, and System Design, Engineering, and Integration. These tasks are executed laterally with USSF SSC depot and development contractors and with BMC3I stakeholders.

This is a full-time position located at 2424 Garden of the Gods Road in Colorado Springs, CO, with occasional work at Peterson Space Force Base (SFB) and Schriever SFB. The role includes international travel to the SST site near Exmouth, Australia, and the SST SOC in Adelaide, Australia. Telework is available one to two days per week, subject to Government discretion.

you will support the Government Program Manager and provide Advisory and Assistance Services across a wide range of Program Management and Engineering tasks. Duties include, but are not limited to:

Provide acquisition support: assist in developing acquisition strategies, cost estimations, requirements, statements of work, and requests for proposal
Review and provide technical evaluation of vendor proposals for sustainment, contractor re-competes, upgrades and modifications
Prepare and staff required program and contract documents; interact with financial, contract, scheduling, risk management, and execution activities and personnel
Support and draft inputs to sustainment and modification budgets for the US Government program manager; assist in developing annual government budget items and justifications for each in the Comprehensive Cost and Requirement (CCaR) and Sustainment Planning, Execution, and Reporting (SPERS) systems
Coordinate, review and provide input to and comments during the development of system design documentation including technical requirements documents (TRDs), capability description documents (CDDs), capability production documents (CPDs), interface control documents (ICDs), and system specifications
Support the Government at technical interchange meetings (TIMs), design reviews, test readiness reviews, internal staff meetings, Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings, working groups, and informal meetings, interfacing with prime contractor program management and technical personnel
Organize and support working group meetings across multiple organizations; research, provide recommended solutions and/or resolve questions, issues, and risks identified in IPT meetings; develop and provide recommended actions to the Government Program Management team and to Portfolio and Division senior management; coordinate with prime contractors, depot contractors, and Government functional teams
Develop strategies, plans and packages for classified and unclassified document submissions and facilitate associated life cycle cost planning and benefit analyses, partnering, acquisition of data rights, and provisioning, staffing packages through process and final approval
Review and provide relevant critical feedback on contractor prepared schedules, budgets, development and test plans
Provide program oversight support to the Government team; prepare briefings, reports, and informational analyses in support of the Division’s programs; identify and prepare consolidated lessons learned reports from applicable related programs

Other duties as requested by the Government and within the constraints of the S3 contract

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Transformation
new_jobs.description:
Meet Benevity

Benevity is the way the world does good, providing companies (and their employees) with technology to take social action on the issues they care about. Through giving, volunteering, grantmaking, employee resource groups and micro-actions, we help most of the Fortune 100 brands build better cultures and use their power for good. We’re also one of the first B Corporations in Canada, meaning we’re as committed to purpose as we are to profits. We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!

As Project Manager, Migrations, you'll drive delivery of Benevity's major platform migrations and related modernization work that affects clients and internal teams. You’ll work in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP Corporate Strategy & Transformation, and partner daily with Technology and Engineering, Architecture, R&D PMO, Product Management, Product Operations, Client Services, Professional Services, and Marketing/client communications.

We’re not looking for someone to track tasks and send status reports. We want a senior project manager who gets into the work:- someone who learns exactly what is slowing a migration down, from data and cutover to client disruption and cross-system dependencies, where the pain points are, and what the teams could do differently. You’ll move our projects faster and make that speed sustainable. Along the way, you’ll spot the gaps in our current process and help the teams design what comes next.

You’ll also be seen as a leader amongst your peers, finding opportunities to mentor and invest in the rituals of the Transformation team of project managers. You will continue raising the bar on how we plan, communicate and deliver.

What You’ll Do

Lead our migrations from planning through cutover and go-live, keeping scope, timelines, risks and dependencies clear and moving
Get into the detail of how the work actually happens: talk to the people doing it, trace where migrations stall, pinpoint the root causes of delays and rework, and partner with the teams to design, test and roll out better ways of working
Work with Technology and Engineering, Architecture, the corporate project office, Product Management, Product Operations, Client Services and Professional Services to unblock work, resolve issues early and surface trade-offs in scope, capacity and priority to leadership with clear options and recommendations
Turn what you learn on individual projects into repeatable playbooks, templates and tools that make delivery faster and more sustainable
Influence stakeholders at every level, building alignment on plans, timelines and process changes without relying on formal authority
Provide clear, honest reporting to leaders that focuses on insight and next steps, not just status
Share good practice with the other project managers on the Transformation team and help raise the standard of how we plan, communicate and deliver
Keep asking how we can do this better, and bring a continuous improvement mindset to every project

What You’ll Bring

Proven experience managing complex, multi-team software implementation or data migration projects with direct client impact, ideally in a SaaS environment (typically 5+ years of project management experience)
A track record of improving how work gets done, not only tracking it: you can point to processes you diagnosed, redesigned and made stick
Enough technical knowledge to engage with Engineering and Architecture on integrations, data migration, identity and access management and system dependencies
Strong critical thinking and curiosity. You take the time to understand the context, ask thoughtful questions and get to the root of a problem before proposing a fix
The influence to alignTechnology and Engineering, Product, Client Services and Professional Services around a plan, and to hold the line on trade-offs with confidence and respect
Experience sharing good practice with, or mentoring, other project managers or team members
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain complex topics to technical and non-technical audiences
Comfort working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment with changing priorities and a globally distributed team
Familiarity with project management tools and methods such as Jira, Confluence and an ability to cross between Agile & Waterfall teams.
Potential knockout criteria (must haves): hands-on experience leading software implementation or data migration projects, and experience identifying and fixing process gaps on those projects

Discover your purpose at work

We’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. From all locations, backgrounds and walks of life, who deserve more …

Innovative work. Growth opportunities. Caring co-workers. And a chance to do work that fills us with a sense of purpose.

If the idea of working on tech that helps people do good in the world lights you up ... If you want a career where you’re valued for who you are and challenged to see who you can become …

It’s time to join Benevity. We’re so excited to meet you.

Where We Work

At Benevity, we embrace a flexible hybrid approach to where we work that empowers our people in a way that supports great work, strong relationships, and personal well-being. For those located near one of our offices, while there’s no set requirement for in-office time, we do value the moments when coming together in person helps us build connection and collaboration. Whether it’s for onboarding, project work, or a chance to align and bond as a team, we trust our people to make thoughtful decisions about when showing up in person matters most.

Join a Company Where DEIB Isn’t a Buzzword

Diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging are part of Benevity’s DNA. You’ll see the impact of our massive investment in DEIB daily — from our well-supported employee resources groups to the exceptional diversity on our leadership and tech teams.

We know that diverse backgrounds, experiences, skills and passions are what move our business and our people forward, so we're committed to creating a culture of belonging with equal opportunities for everyone to shine.

That starts with a fair and accessible hiring process. If you want to feel seen, heard and celebrated, you belong at Benevity.

Candidates with disabilities who may require accommodations throughout the hiring or assessment process are encouraged to reach out to accommodations@benevity.com.

Who You’ll Work With

Nike is committed to creating a safe and compliant work environment for our employees, partners, and communities. Ensuring that the machines and equipment used in manufacturing and innovation operations are safely designed, installed, and operated is foundational to manufacturing safety.

The Machine Safety Program Manager reports directly to the EHS Director, AirMI & Innovation. This role partners across engineering, innovation, manufacturing operations, maintenance, facilities and learning and development as well as Nike’s Global Machine Safety Steering Committee to build consistent and sustainable machine safety practices worldwide.

Who We Are Looking For

Nike is looking for a Machine Safety subject matter expert who can translate complex technical and regulatory requirements into practical programs that protect people throughout the equipment lifecycle. This person brings deep experience in machine guarding, electrical safety, hazardous energy control, robotics and emerging manufacturing technologies. They understand how to design safety into equipment from concept through installation and operation rather than addressing it after the fact.

The successful candidate combines technical depth with strong business judgment and the ability to influence cross functions. They can independently lead complex global programs while building trust across engineering, manufacturing and operational teams. They bring a disciplined, analytical approach and can prioritize effectively in a fast-moving, matrixed environment. They connect technical safety requirements with machine development, manufacturing operations and business planning across the full equipment lifecycle while aligning with global programs. Just as importantly, they communicate directly and thoughtfully and bring a proactive approach to identifying risks before those risks become incidents.

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Environment, Health & Safety, Engineering or related field. Will accept any suitable combination of education, experience and training.
8 to10 years of machine and equipment safety experience, preferably within manufacturing, engineering or industrial environment.
Demonstrated expertise applying National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) requirements and relevant consensus safety standards to industrial machines and equipment.
Experience developing and implementing safety programs and technical training with proficiency in root cause investigations, corrective and preventive actions and continuous improvement.
Experience with robotics, Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) or other emerging manufacturing technologies preferred. Relevant technical safety certifications are also preferred.

What You’ll Work On

As part of the EHS team, you’ll shape how machine safety is designed into Nike’s manufacturing and innovation environment. Working across technical and operational teams, you’ll build programs that are scalable, auditable and adaptable to local regulatory requirements while supporting consistent global safety expectations.

You'll play an instrumental role in developing and implementing a comprehensive machine safety program which integrates federal, state, and local regulations as well as industry-leading standards into the equipment and machines used in manufacturing and innovation.

Develop and sustain Nike’s machine safety program across AirMI, Innovation and manufacturing operations with controls covering machine guarding, electrical safety, lockout/tagout, robotics, Autonomous Mobile Robots, lasers and radiation.
Build a comprehensive stage-gate safety process across the equipment lifecycle and participate in design reviews, risk assessments, Factory Acceptance Tests and Site Acceptance Tests for new machinery and equipment.
Establish and sustain auditable machine safety practices including equipment-specific lockout/tagout procedures, electrical labeling and controls for robotics, Autonomous Mobile Robots and radiation hazards.
Partner with engineering, operations, maintenance, facilities and learning and development teams to integrate technical safety requirements and hazardous-energy controls into equipment design, operating practices and training.
Lead machine-related incident and near-miss root cause investigations and drive corrective and preventive actions through timely closure while sharing learnings that can strengthen safety across the organization.
Serve as the machine safety subject matter expert for continuous-improvement initiatives, internal and external audits and inspections while helping responsible teams resolve findings and strengthen controls.
Monitor machine and equipment safety Key Performance Indicators and provide analysis to leadership while ensuring machine, equipment and Autonomous Mobile Robot safety requirements are considered in facility and asset planning.

new_jobs.title: IT Security Manager* (Risk & Resilience)
new_jobs.description:
Mit rund 6.300 Mitarbeitern und zahlreichen Produktionsstandorten im In- und Ausland gehören wir zu den führenden Unternehmensgruppen für Farben, Lacke, Bautenschutz und energiesparende Wärmedämm-Verbundsysteme in Europa. Unser Hauptsitz befindet sich im Rhein-Main-Gebiet. Im Profi- und auch DIY-Geschäft sind wir mit unseren bekannten Marken Caparol
und Alpina
Marktführer.
Zur weiteren Verstärkung unseres mehrköpfigen IT-Cyber-Security-Teams suchen wir dich als
IT Security Manager* (Risk & Resilience)

Du möchtest Informationssicherheit nicht nur verwalten, sondern aktiv weiterentwickeln?
In dieser Rolle etablierst du Prozesse und Standards und gestaltest die gruppenweite Weiterentwicklung von Informationssicherheit, IT-Risikomanagement und Business Continuity innerhalb der DAW aktiv mit. Gemeinsam mit IT-Teams, Fachbereichen und weiteren Stakeholdern sorgst du dafür, dass Risiken frühzeitig erkannt, Sicherheitsanforderungen nachhaltig verankert und kritische Geschäftsprozesse bestmöglich abgesichert werden.
In dieser Rolle sind Homeoffice und mobiles Arbeiten innerhalb Deutschlands an insgesamt 9 Tagen/Monat möglich (auf Basis einer Vollzeittätigkeit).
(*) Bei DAW zählt der Mensch. So bunt wie unsere Farben und so vielfältig wie unsere Marken sind auch die Menschen, die bei uns arbeiten. Ob Alter, Geschlecht, Hautfarbe, Herkunft, Sprache oder Religion: Bei uns wird kein Unterschied gemacht. Bei uns kann jeder Teil der DAW-Familie werden, der unsere Vision von gesunden und nachhaltigen Lebensräumen mitgestalten möchte.

Aufgaben

Du erkennst IT- und Cyber-Risiken frühzeitig, bewertest deren Auswirkungen und schaffst Transparenz für Management und relevante Stakeholder.
Unser IT-Risikomanagement entwickelst du kontinuierlich weiter, pflegst das IT-Risk-Register und sorgst dafür, dass vereinbarte Maßnahmen zur Risikobehandlung wirksam umgesetzt werden.
Cyber-Bedrohungen, Sicherheitswarnungen und regulatorische Entwicklungen analysierst du und leitest daraus konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen für die DAW-Gruppe ab.
Du treibst die Weiterentwicklung unseres IT-Business-Continuity-Management-Systems (IT-BCMS) voran und stellst sicher, dass kritische IT-Services auch in Ausnahmesituationen zuverlässig verfügbar bleiben.
Business-Impact-Analysen, Incident-Simulationen, Recovery-Tests und weitere Resilienzmaßnahmen planst, koordinierst und begleitest du eigenständig.
Gemeinsam mit dem Cyber-Security-Team entwickelst du unser Information Security Management System (ISMS) kontinuierlich weiter und bringst neue Impulse für praxisnahe Sicherheitslösungen ein.
Als Sparringspartner für IT-Projekte, Fachbereiche und internationale Gesellschaften berätst du zu Informationssicherheit, Business Continuity und regulatorischen Anforderungen wie NIS2, SWIFT oder Vorgaben aus Cyber-Versicherungen.
Außerdem unterstützt du bei der Umsetzung und Koordination regulatorischer sowie interner Sicherheitsanforderungen, beispielsweise im Umfeld von NIS2, SWIFT, Cyber-Versicherungen und weiteren Compliance-Vorgaben.

Profil

Du hast ein Studium der (Wirtschafts-)Informatik, IT-Sicherheit oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation erfolgreich abgeschlossen und bringst mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Umfeld von IT-Security, IT-Risk-Management, Business-Continuity-Management oder vergleichbaren Governance-, Risk- und Compliance-Funktionen mit.
Mit relevanten Standards und Frameworks wie ISO 27001, ISO 22301, BSI 200-4, NIS2 oder vergleichbaren Ansätzen bist du vertraut und kannst deren Anforderungen praxisnah in den Unternehmensalltag übertragen.
Du verfügst über ein gutes Verständnis moderner IT-Infrastrukturen, geschäftskritischer Prozesse sowie gängiger Security-Technologien und Sicherheitsmechanismen.
Risiken und komplexe Zusammenhänge analysierst du strukturiert, denkst lösungsorientiert und leitest daraus pragmatische Maßnahmen ab.
Die Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern macht dir Spaß, und du überzeugst durch deine Beratungskompetenz.
Dich zeichnet ein hohes Maß an integrativer und gleichermaßen durchsetzungsstarker Kommunikationsfähigkeit in deutscher und – im Rahmen internationaler Zusammenarbeit – englischer Sprache aus.

Wir bieten

Jobs, in denen du was bewegen kannst

Gemeinsam mit dir gestalten wir die Zukunft nachhaltigen Bauens. Mach mit deinen Ideen und deiner Schaffenskraft die Welt bunter, schöner, nachhaltiger – und lebenswerter!
Inhabergeführtes Familienunternehmen

DAW ist zu 100 % im Besitz der Familie Murjahn und das spürt man. Mittlerweile in der fünften Generation inhabergeführt, geht es bei uns nicht um den schnellen Gewinn, sondern um langfristiges und nachhaltiges Wachstum. Bei uns arbeiten Familien, Geschwister und Verwandte generationsübergreifend Tür an Tür.
Freiraum, mitzugestalten

Weil wir möchten, dass du deine Potenziale voll entfalten kannst, bieten wir dir viel Platz, deine Ideen einzubringen und umzusetzen. Entweder „on the Job“ oder im Rahmen eines unserer zahlreichen Innovations-Formate. Außerdem beziehen wir dich in Entscheidungen mit ein und berücksichtigen dabei deine Bedürfnisse.
Nachhaltigkeit in allen Belangen

Für uns ist Nachhaltigkeit kein Modewort, sondern Teil unserer DNA. Schon sehr früh haben wir erkannt, dass nachhaltiger Erfolg nur möglich ist, wenn wir im Einklang mit der Umwelt und ressourcenschonend handeln. Nachhaltiges Handeln zeigt sich sowohl in unserer Klimastrategie als auch in unserer langfristigen und nachhaltigen Geschäfts- und Produktphilosophie. Nachhaltig sind auch die Beziehungen zu unseren Mitarbeitern, die uns teilweise schon mehr als 30 Jahre die Treue halten.
Flexibles Arbeiten: Mehr Zeit für Hobbys und Familie

An unseren Standorten bieten wir dir je nach Bereich und Tätigkeit unterschiedliche Arbeitszeitmodelle an. Wo immer möglich, setzen wir auf Flexibilität durch Gleitzeit und mobiles Arbeiten.
Gehalt: Mehr als nur 12 Monatsgehälter

Als tariflicher Mitarbeiter profitierst du von unserem Haustarif, der sich am Chemietarif orientiert. Und damit nicht nur von attraktiven 12 Monatsgehältern, sondern auch von Urlaubs- und Weihnachtsgeld. Für unsere außertariflichen Angestellten gelten gesonderte Leistungen. Dein genaues Gehalt ist abhängig von der jeweiligen Stelle und deinen individuellen Voraussetzungen und wird abschließend errechnet.
Betriebliche Gesundheitsförderung

Unser Programm zur betrieblichen Gesundheitsförderung berücksichtigt alle Aspekte deiner Gesundheit und basiert auf den vier Kernmodulen Bewegung, Ernährung, Entspannung und Prävention. Das Programm wird ständig erweitert.

Important note

Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered.

Status:
Temporary, Full-Time (12 months)

Work Location:

Who We Are

The British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (“BCCNM”) is the college empowered under the Health Professions and Occupations Act (HPOA) to regulate the practice of all licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, registered midwives, registered nurses, and registered psychiatric nurses in British Columbia. Regulation helps to protect the public by ensuring that professional care or service received by the public is competent, ethical, and meets the standards that society views as acceptable.

As western Canada’s largest health profession regulator, we believe a diverse and inclusive team enriches our efforts to protect the public. We welcome applications from all who reflect of the communities we serve and especially encourage Indigenous Peoples and members of equity-seeking groups to apply. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences bring both innovation and better outcomes to the work we do and the decisions we make.

BCCNM’s commitment to Indigenous Specific Anti-Racism

BCCNM is committed to working with Indigenous Peoples and health system partners to support Indigenous-specific anti-racist practices in the health system. As the largest health regulator in Western Canada, BCCNM has the opportunity to influence the health professionals we regulate, as well as the broader health-care system, to break the cycle of racism, and improve health outcomes for Indigenous Peoples. BCCNM has pledged to become culturally safe and anti-racist, and to support the health professionals we regulate to do the same.

What We Offer You

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner. The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 - $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income after 1 year of employment. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. Our office is closed for the 11 statutory holidays in B.C. as well as Easter Monday and Boxing Day.

What You’ll Be Doing

Reporting to the Manager, Project & Portfolio Management, The Project Manager II (PMII) liaises with internal and external business stakeholders and/or technical teams in managing the scope, schedule, resourcing, communication, and issue escalation for assigned projects. Maintains effective working relationships with and manages expectations of all stakeholders across the organization. Enables and supports a transparent, accountable, and collaborative working culture through the overall project processes.

Demonstrates a commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and supporting organizational actions towards addressing indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.

Flexible, able to quickly adapt to unfamiliar, ambiguous, or changing conditions.

The Meta Infra Technical Program Management (TPM) community is pioneering technologies to bring people and businesses closer together at a global scale. Infra TPMs are the enablers for our toughest business strategies to become technical realities, requiring direct and close partnership with both Engineering and Product teams to make products come to life with incredible scale, reliability, and efficiency.Meta's infrastructure software stack is being upgraded for a world where the primary consumer of our platforms is an agent, not a human at a terminal, and our core infrastructure stack is being upgraded for the rigor, speed, and scale required of modern training, inferencing, and app development. These shifts change how we design APIs and interfaces, how we onboard and support internal and external partners, how we plan features, and how we measure adoption and success. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own that transformation for a major surface of Meta's Infra software stack.In this role, you will partner with Engineering and Product leadership to shape the technical roadmap for the platforms you own, drive the design and rollout of the interfaces those platforms expose, and own end-to-end delivery and adoption with the partner teams who build on top of them. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy on ambiguous, cross-organizational problems turning open-ended strategic questions into concrete programs with a credible path to success and you will set the technical program management standard for the teams around you.

Technical Program Manager, Infrastructure Software Systems Responsibilities:

Own technical program management for a core area of Meta's infrastructure software stack, spanning platform strategy, technical design, delivery, and partner adoption
Partner with Engineering and Product to define the multi-quarter roadmap: shaping feature plans, participating substantively in technical design and API/interface design reviews, and making tradeoff recommendations that leadership acts on
Drive platform adoption end to end — defining the onboarding path for partner teams, removing friction in integration, and holding the bar on the partner experience from first evaluation through steady-state production use
Translate the needs of demanding internal customer organizations into platform requirements, and broker the prioritization conversations required to land them
Define and instrument the metrics that determine whether the platform is succeeding — adoption, reliability, efficiency, and developer/agent effectiveness — and use them to drive decisions rather than to report status
Lead technical discussions and act as a thought leader in program and design reviews
be the cross-functional partner engineering leaders pull into their hardest problems
Identify and solve systemic problems that span organizational boundaries, and build the lightweight operational constructs that accelerate team momentum without adding overhead
Perform risk assessment, risk mitigation, and change management across a portfolio of concurrent technical programs
Articulate technical vision, requirements, goals, and milestones to stakeholders up to and including VP-level leadership
Provide hands-on program management through design, development, testing, rollout, and post-launch phases
Mentor and raise the bar for other technical program managers, and influence how TPM is practiced across the broader organization

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience
10+ years of experience in software, systems, or hardware engineering, or technical product/program management
Experience delivering technical programs or products from inception through to delivery
Knowledge of user needs assessment, requirements gathering, and scope definition
Experience working autonomously across multiple teams, demonstrating critical thinking and thought leadership
Experience communicating and collaborating with technical management teams to develop systems, solutions, and products
Experience in organization, coordination, and prioritization of competing workstreams
Experience in analytical thinking and problem-solving applied to large-scale systems
Experience establishing and maintaining working relationships across multidisciplinary teams and with partners in multiple time zones

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience partnering with large internal customer organizations to migrate them onto a shared platform
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Model Delivery
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own model delivery.

Every model we ship, whether we trained it or brought it in from a partner, has to be selected on evaluation criteria, integrated and routed across the product stack, and adhere to regulatory requirements; released to customer environments ready for general availability. That now happens on a monthly cadence, with several model evaluations a week, and each release goes out to our platform partners.

This is a standing program, with one owner from model candidate to GA. You will join Product Engineering Program Management and work across modeling, evaluation, inference serving, engineering, customer delivery.

At Cohere, Technical Program Managers are the operational owners of cross-functional work. The best of them are precise at the tactical level and useful at the strategic one: organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic, and able to change pace when the program does.

As a Technical Program Manager, You Will

Own the path from model candidate to general availability for first-party and third-party models, on a monthly cadence.
Build one release process across modeling, evaluation, product integration, and customer delivery, with an owner, exit criteria, and lead time for each stage.
Run a delivery-readiness gate that has to pass before general availability: packaging, signed images and digests, documentation, serving configuration, test coverage, and parity across Platform, Model Vault, and private deployments.
Work with Safety and Legal to build regulatory checkpoints into the model release pipeline, including EU AI Act systemic-risk obligations. Program manage the recurring compliance calendar post launch: the yearly review of our frontier framework, serious-incident reporting deadlines, and access for external evaluators.
Stand up a model registry the field, partner teams and regulators can answer from, covering name, route, alias, checkpoint, sizing, serving configuration, and where each model is available.
Run intake for new models, keep the pipeline visible, and drive the selection decision to the right owner by a date, with a decision log of which models enter the lineup.
Sequence deprecation and partner notices on a calendar agreed with customer and partner teams.
Make the monthly model lineup change a routine step in North, including routing and availability, and feed model readiness into the product release train.
Build the mechanisms that make the cadence repeatable: templates, the registry, automation, and retros that change the system.
Write the status, the decision, and the external notice so executives, engineers, and partners are working from the same answer.

You May Be a Good Fit If You

Have at least 8 years as an Engineering or Technical Program Manager, including ownership of repeatable launches with readiness checklists, go/no-go gates, and rollback criteria that teams actually used.
Can discuss model serving and deployment at a working level: GPU sizing, tensor parallelism, quantization, speculative decoding, containers, Kubernetes and Helm, image signing, and air-gapped or private deployment. Enough to spot conflicting answers and know who decides.
Drive open questions (name, alias, default, sizing) to the owner who should decide them, by a date, and then publish the answer.
Influence without authority across research, engineering, product, and the field.
Write clearly for executives, engineers, and external partners, including customer and partner notices.
Are comfortable at a high cadence, with shifting priorities and overlapping launches.
Can read evaluation results and a cost-versus-performance tradeoff, and can tell when a benchmark does not answer the product question.

Helpful, And Not Required

Launch experience at a model provider or an AI platform.
Familiarity with the ML lifecycle: evaluations, checkpoints, provenance, and serving stacks such as vLLM.
Experience running launches under regulation or an AI management standard, such as the EU AI Act or ISO 42001.
Experience with model routing, AI gateways, or agent platforms.
Enterprise software delivery to regulated customers.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

Job Description:

IT - Cybersecurity Solution Security Analyst

Location:
McLean, Virginia (Hybrid)

Alternate Location:
Dallas, Texas; Memphis, Tennessee

Role Overview

An established organization seeks a technically grounded cybersecurity professional to assess proposed technologies, enterprise applications, artificial intelligence solutions, cloud platforms, and third-party vendors prior to production use. This position serves in a technical advisory and assessment capacity, focusing on security reviews rather than hands-on engineering, security operations center operations, audit, or traditional governance, risk, and compliance. The successful candidate will leverage technical breadth to evaluate how systems are constructed, analyze data exchange mechanisms, identify potential vulnerabilities, formulate evidence requests, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Perform comprehensive cybersecurity reviews and provide security guidance for business and technology initiatives to ensure alignment with security standards.
Assess internal and external applications, vendor solutions, APIs, integrations, cloud services, identity architectures, and data flows throughout the solution lifecycle.
Develop and maintain solution security artifacts, including architecture reviews, data flow diagrams, security requirements, and implementation guidance.
Communicate security risks, trade-offs, and mitigation strategies to technical and non-technical stakeholders to enable informed business decisions.
Coordinate assessments with the governance, risk, and compliance team, which manages formal risk registry functions.
Define review scope, identify security requirements, and ensure necessary validation activities are completed.
Evaluate architecture artifacts, including network diagrams, data flow diagrams, integration patterns, API designs, vulnerability assessments, and assessment documentation.
Identify security gaps, document risks, identify compensating controls, and support remediation efforts prior to production release.
Contribute to the evolution of security standards, reference architectures, secure development practices, and governance processes.

Required Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience:
Approximately 5 to 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology, software engineering, solution architecture, risk assessment, or a related discipline, with at least 5 years assessing or delivering applications, cloud services, integrations, APIs, or enterprise technology solutions.

Technical Skills:
Strong understanding of modern application security, cloud security practices, and secure software development lifecycles. Working knowledge of networking concepts and controls, including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, and network segmentation. Proven ability to interpret network, architecture, and data-flow diagrams to identify potential security issues.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience evaluating security risks in artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence systems, including model integration and data governance.
Prior experience supporting hospitality, travel, e-commerce, payments, financial services, or other large-scale customer-facing platforms.
Industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, AWS Certified Security - Specialty, or AWS Certified Solutions Architect.
Familiarity with regulatory and industry frameworks, including PCI DSS, GDPR, CCPA, NIST 800-53, SOC 2, and ISO 27001.
Experience utilizing AuditBoard or ServiceNow workflow platforms.
